title: Coffee and Arterial Stiffness Evaluation
official: Coffee and Arterial Stiffness: Effects on Chronic Coffee Intake on Markers of Vascular Function, Cardiometabolic and Liver Health
summary: This study aims to investigate whether twelve weeks of daily coffee consumption can improve blood vessel elasticity (arterial stiffness) in adults typical of the UK population who are currently non-habitual coffee consumers. Additionally, the effects on cardiometabolic disease risk markers, liver health markers, cognitive function and inter-individual genetic variations in response to coffee consumption will be examined.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Males and females
* Aged between 40 to 75 years
* Low habitual coffee consumption (less than 3 cups per week) (over the past 4-week period)
* Body mass index (BMI) between 18.5-32.0kg/m\^2 (inclusive)
* Total cholesterol ≤6.5 mmol/L
* Fasting triglycerides \<1.7 mmol/L
* Fasting glucose ≤ 6.1 mmol/L
* Blood pressure 90/60 - 140/90 mmHg (inclusive)

Exclusion Criteria:

* Sensitivity to coffee or caffeine
* Regular consumption of caffeinated products or drinks; including tea, energy drinks or caffeine tablets (over 350 mg caffeine per week) or unwilling to stop drinking coffee during the intervention period
* Current smoking and vaping use
* Medical history of chronic diseases (cancer, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, ischaemic attacks and/or any other cardiovascular related diseases, gastro-intestinal disorders, hyperlipidaemia, kidney or liver disease)
* Haemoglobin \<115 g/L for females or \<130 g/L for males
* Prescribed any medication relating to the study outcome measures (such as blood pressure lowering, anti-inflammatories or blood thinners)
* Current use or past use of antibiotics within 6 months
* Drinking more than the recommended intake for alcohol (\>14 units of alcohol per week)
* Current undertaking or planning to start a weight reducing regimen
* Taking any supplements (vitamins, minerals, prebiotics and probiotics)
* Any other medical history or diet and lifestyle habits or practices that would preclude volunteers from participating in a dietary intervention and metabolic study (e.g. pacemaker)
* Parallel participation in another intervention study
* Pregnancy, planning a pregnancy in the next 6 months or breastfeeding
* NHS blood donation (470 ml) in the last 3 months
